package.name: autoware_tracking_speed_guard
package.description:
Slows the robot down while it is tracking the trajectory badly.
The node runs alongside the trajectory follower: it takes the same inputs the controller takes -- the trajectory the controller is following and the vehicle odometry -- and computes the same two quantities the MPC computes, the lateral error and the heading error against the nearest point of that trajectory. The difference is the output: the MPC steers, this node only lowers a speed limit.
Nothing else in the stack does this. The MPC has no error threshold at all and no way to influence speed, and the planning validator's deviation checks are configured with thresholds that never trip. So a robot that has been left far from its path -- after a recovery manoeuvre, say -- chases it at full speed.
The limit is published on the external velocity limit channel under its own sender name, so it composes with every other limit in the system rather than overriding them. It is released only once BOTH errors have been small for a while.
Forward and reverse missions are treated identically: the heading error is measured against the direction of travel taken from the trajectory's velocity sign, exactly as the MPC does, so one definition holds in both motion modes.
